title: Usage review rules
description: Declarations the usage review evaluates against the record. Each rule is a sentence a person can read in a sitting: over these subjects, in this window, above this floor, when this holds, the cause is this well known, and this is what it usually means. A gate the vocabulary cannot express is not a rule - there are no coded rules.

id.description: The rule's name, and the name of its provenance file. Cited by a triage PR's provenance entry, so it is an identifier rather than a description.

over.description: What the rule judges one at a time. `checks` is the scope totals rather than a rule, so such a rule yields at most one finding.

expect.description: Narrows a skill rule to skills declaring that expectation of themselves. Absent, the rule judges every skill - including the ones that declare nothing.

window.description: `28 days` is the trailing window, with `previous.` naming the 28 before it; `adoption` is the subject pack's own adoption window; `now` is a live read of the tree, which no window applies to.

floor.description: Counts that must hold before the rule is evaluated at all. Under the floor the review records *not evaluated* with the figure, which is what keeps a young window from reading as a clean one.

when.description: One comparison, in four shapes: `a / b >= n`, `a / b <= n`, `a = 0`, `a >= n`. `median(a)` takes the median across the window's days and `previous.` reads the window before. Nothing else - a rule needing more is not a rule.

and.description: A live predicate the record cannot answer - a name (`proseTwin`) or one more comparison against a live figure (`tokens <= 300`). Both sides must hold.

cause.description: How well the record alone settles the cause: `known` where the arithmetic or the mechanism leaves one, `probable` where one is likeliest, `unknown` where the finding is evidence only. It tells a reader what the recommendation is worth, and nothing follows from it automatically except which findings the triage may act on.

causes.description: The possible causes in likelihood order, each with the discriminator that tells it apart. For a `known` rule this is what the arithmetic already settled; otherwise it is the search order a reader works through.

open.description: True where the list is only what its authors thought of, so a reader may find a cause not on it; false where the mechanism closes it.

finding.description: The sentence a person reads as the finding.

recommendation.description: The sentence a person reads as what it usually means. `none` where the finding is evidence carried forward and nothing is proposed.
